ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, six rays OA, OB, OC, OD, OE, and OF are drawn from point O, and $\angle AOB=90^\circ$, OF bisects $\angle BOC$, OE bisects $\angle AOD$. If $\angle EOF=170^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle COD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the problem, we have \\
\(\because \angle AOB=90^\circ\), \(\angle EOF=170^\circ\), \\
\(\therefore \angle AOE + \angle FOB = 360^\circ - 90^\circ - 170^\circ = 100^\circ\). \\
\(\because\) OF bisects \(\angle COB\), OE bisects \(\angle AOD\), \\
\(\therefore \angle COF = \angle FOB\), \(\angle AOE = \angle EOD\). \\
\(\therefore \angle EOD + \angle COF = 100^\circ\). \\
\(\therefore \angle COD = 170^\circ - 100^\circ = \boxed{70^\circ}\).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, all six rays start from point O, OA points to the left, OB points upward, and a right-angle mark is used to indicate that ∠AOB=90°; the order around O in the figure can be regarded as A-B-F-C-D-E-A, in which OF is located between OB and OC, and OE is located between OD and OA. The problem statement also gives that OF bisects ∠BOC, OE bisects ∠AOD, and ∠EOF=170°. Reasoning: Looking at one full circle around point O as 360°, after the known ∠AOB=90° and ∠EOF=170° from OE to OF passing through D and C occupy their parts, the two remaining parts are exactly ∠AOE and ∠BOF, so ∠AOE+∠BOF=360°-90°-170°=100°. Also because OE bisects ∠AOD, ∠AOE=∠EOD; because OF bisects ∠BOC, ∠BOF=∠FOC. Therefore ∠EOD+∠COF is also equal to 100°. And ∠EOF=∠EOD+∠COD+∠COF=170°, so ∠COD=170°-100°=70°.
